text.p: Lehman Brothers initiated coverage of Dead Sea Bromine with a 2-Outperform rating, saying the Israeli company is set to experience strong sustainable growth from new business activities.

"The company has benefited from increased profitability due to investing in new products, entering new business areas within its core operations and expanding capacity to produce raw materials to achieve economies of scale," analyst Elise Horowitz said in a report released on Wednesday.
Lehman estimates the company will earn $0.41 a share in 1997 and $0.50 in 1998 against $0.36 in 1996.
The shares, trading at 21.66 shekels, have risen over 40 percent in the past year.
"DSB is a low-risk investment...We see continued upside potential in the shares of up to 22 percent and see them trading between 24.34-26.75 over the next 12 months," the report said.
The company, a subsidiary of Israel Chemicals, is the world's largest producer of bromine.
